staged_as_one_operation.mechanics: one SSM invocation: refuse if /opt/mr002/v35 exists; decode the archive; verify its sha256 AFTER transfer before extracting; extract; copy the v34 inputs; patch the two scalars; re-read and hash.
staged_as_one_operation.why: v3.2 staged code and configuration independently, a stale configuration went undetected, and the run spent a governed opening while declaring an identity that was not the one executing. Archive and configuration now land together or not at all.

staged_configuration.guard: the patch refused unless EXACTLY two occurrences of the superseded identity were present, and refused on any CR byte before or after the write.
staged_configuration.how_it_was_changed: PATCHED, not replaced: a literal substitution of the two 64-hex identity scalars, leaving every other byte untouched. The staged config is NOT the ExecutionConfiguration - it also carries run_id, window, runtime_facts and the sealed input digests - and a JSON round-trip would have rewritten bytes no ruling authorised anyone to touch. The byte length is unchanged at 3896 precisely because the substitution is hex-for-hex.

supersedes.why: v3.4 aborted the whole run at candidate construction on a corporate-action row whose economics had no bearing on it. The bridge, not the producer, was defective.
